ui_bugs.issue: React error 'Maximum update depth exceeded. This can happen when a component calls setState inside useEffect, but useEffect either doesn't have a dependency array, or one of the dependencies changes on every render.' fires repeatedly the moment the Won tab is opened (67 rows of ClickToInvoiceLink). The page still renders the rows visually, but the render is in a feedback loop. Likely cause: a useEffect in ClickToInvoiceLink (or a child) with an object/function dep that is rebuilt every render, or a parent passing a non-memoised prop. Triage: inspect ClickToInvoiceLink.jsx useEffect deps + the props passed from MyQuotesPage row map.

context_for_next_testing_agent: All iter26 backend tests pass. The 4 user-reported asks are functionally working in the UI. The ONE outstanding issue is a React 'Maximum update depth exceeded' error on /my-quotes Won tab caused by ClickToInvoiceLink (or its consumer). Trigger: login as pro@test.com, navigate to /my-quotes, click the 'Won' tab. The 67 rows still paint, so the visual contract for issue (2) is met, but the infinite-render warning is a release-blocker for performance. After the main agent fixes the dep array in ClickToInvoiceLink, re-test by counting [data-testid$='-locked'] occurrences = 67.
rca of the issue: MyQuotesPage maps 67 won quotes to <ClickToInvoiceLink quote={q} job={...} hasToolkit={hasToolkit} />. Each render rebuilds the inline objects/job lookup, and any useEffect inside ClickToInvoiceLink that depends on the full object (rather than a stable id) will retrigger every render → setState → re-render → useEffect → … infinite loop. Fix: depend only on primitive ids (e.g., quote.id, quote.status, job.status), or memoise the row props in the parent's .map() with useMemo per id. Backend is unaffected; the loop is purely client-side.
